case_summary: A transport logger must resume recording after power loss and ensure exports never silently omit readings the display called recorded.
answer: The current ordering cannot meet the request: it labels a sample before buffered append, and flush has no documented power-loss durability. Define ‘recorded’ as a durable commit. The smallest complete change is a storage commit boundary: append a framed record with sequence number and checksum, invoke a storage operation whose contract guarantees persistence, then show the sample as recorded. On boot/export, accept only complete valid frames and verify sequence continuity; if corruption or a gap is found, surface an explicit incomplete-export error rather than copying a silently truncated file. A partial final frame can be discarded because it was never acknowledged. This requires a card/controller durability guarantee (or different storage hardware); framing and flush alone cannot provide it. If no such guarantee is available, the device must not display ‘recorded’ at all—only ‘sampled’/‘pending’—and must report uncertainty after interruption. Still decide the maximum sampling delay, whether to stop sampling or mark unsaved samples when storage is full, and the exact display state that constitutes acknowledgement. The guarantee covers acknowledged samples only; samples taken but not durably committed at the instant of power loss may be lost. Verify by cutting power around append/commit/display boundaries, filling/removing the card, and checking that every acknowledged sequence appears in a validated export or export fails visibly. Exact guarantees depend on the selected storage’s documented durability semantics.
